ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached graph plots pH on the vertical axis against volume of NaOH added in mL on the horizontal axis. The titration curve for carbonic acid has two major steep rising regions, corresponding to two equivalence points, with flatter buffer-like regions between and after them. Reasoning: The carbonic acid sample is unchanged when the titration is repeated, so the number of moles of NaOH needed to reach each equivalence point is unchanged. Increasing the concentration of NaOH means each milliliter contains more moles of NaOH. Since volume needed equals required moles divided by NaOH concentration, a higher NaOH concentration requires a smaller volume to supply the same moles. Therefore both equivalence points would occur at lower NaOH volumes, shifting left on the graph.
